questions.question:
**The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

The birds flew / fastly above us / as we stood / on our terrace.
questions.solution:
The segment that contains a grammatical error is **'****fastly above'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **‘Fastly’** is **not correct.**
 
• The word** ‘fast’ is used in the same form in adjectives and in adverbs.**
 
• Generally, we **add ' ly' to the adjectives to change them into adverbs.**
 
• But there are certain words that can be used **as adjectives as well as adverbs without adding 'ly'.** **Eg:** ‘ fast, straight, enough, etc. ‘
 
• **Examples-** * • He ran fast. (adverb)*

* •They like fast cars and expensive restaurants. (adjective)*

So, the right sentence is**:** *The birds flew fast above us as we stood on our terrace.__*

The correct answer is **option 3.**

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.**

She said, “I can play the guitar pretty well.”

options.text: She said that she can play the guitar pretty well.
She said that she would play the guitar pretty well
She said that she could play the guitar pretty well.
She said that she plays the guitar pretty well.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **She said that she could play the guitar pretty well.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is in **direct speech** and we need to convert it to** indirect speech.**
 
• When we change a direct speech to indirect speech, we must follow these **rules:**

​ **•** The reporting verb** 'said' **remains unchanged.

 **•** The** inverted commas ("...")** are replaced with the conjunction **'that'** to show the indirect speech.

 **•** **A comma (,)** that is added after the direct speech part, **should be removed** in the indirect speech.

 **•** The modal **'can'** changes to **'could'.**

 **• 'I'** changes to **'she'.**

 
• Thus, **option 3** is the correct answer.

Hence, The Indirect speech is- ***She said that she could play the guitar pretty well.***

questions.question:

questions.question:
**Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.**

A. When the fish, at last, had been safely landed, I asked the brothers if they ate fish.

B. The condition that I put was that they had to help me land another fish for my men.

C. On receiving their eager answer that they most certainly did, I told them I would give them the fish we had just landed.

D. To this they readily agreed and the wait started again.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"ACBD"**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Let's look at the correct sequence of the passage.
 
• **Statement A** is the **opening sentence** of the passage which explains the theme of the passage what happened when the narrator landed and his worry about the fish.
 
• **Statement C** is **the second sentence** of the passage.
 
• **Statement B** is the** third sentence** of the passage which explains the deal and how they agreed to the narrator's condition.
 
• **Statement D** is the **last sentence** of the passage and also an extensive portion of the previous statement that the condition made by the narrator.​

​Hence, the correct sequence is** A, C, B, D**

The correct passage is**:** **A.** When the fish, at last, had been safely landed, I asked the brothers if they ate fish. **C.** On receiving the eager answer that they most certainly did, I told them I would give them the fish we had just landed. **B.** The condition that I put was that they had to help me land another fish for my men. **D.** To this they readily agreed and the wait started again.
